text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: P1 - inference-host-pool-us-east-1 - elevated 5xx and timeouts, root cause suspected GPU host instability (gpu-host-123). Paging @sre_oncall and infra.

sre_oncall: I got the page — acknowledging. Pulling dashboards now. Any immediate customer hits?

mira: Seeing spike in error rate for model-runner pods on node gpu-host-123 around 01:22 UTC. Multiple pods restarted. k8s shows node NotReady then rebooted.

jordan: I'm on infra. Checking node diagnostics. Kube events: "eviction" + "node lost" followed by node reboot. Draining now.

mira: Container logs: repeated NVML errors and driver disconnects. Snippet from dmesg attached below.

mira: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU reported ECC error: device memory
[ 12345.679012] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: 00000001
[ 12345.679200] pcie 0000:65:00.0: AER: Multiple root port resets - resetting link
[ 12345.679456] kernel: nvhost: GPU watchdog timeout - resetting GPU
```

ashley: Started mitigation: routing fallback requests to the dedicated pool (model-small-quant) and increasing retry budget for clients. Should reduce visible errors within a minute. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

luis: CS update: Notified customers A and C. A reported 5xx for approx 3 minutes, C reported degraded latency. Customer B opened a support ticket but no 5xx. I'll keep them updated.

jordan: Drain in progress: `kubectl drain gpu-host-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — pods are gracefully terminating and rescheduling.

infra_bot: Filing cloud provider ticket: Created CP case #CP-78321 (provider: us-east gpu host instability). Attaching dmesg and `nvidia-smi -q` output.

eng_runtime_tanaka: Any recent kernel or driver patches rolled out to the host pool? I see a kernel update in the image from 2026-03-10.

mira: Host boot logs show unplanned reboot at 2026-03-12T01:23:40Z. NVML ECC counts incremented right before reboot. Running `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`:

mira: ```
==============
Ecc Errors
==============
Volatile
    Single Bit ECC errors: 125
    Double Bit ECC errors: 2
Non-Volatile
    Single Bit ECC errors: 0
    Double Bit ECC errors: 0
```

sre_oncall: Hypotheses: 1) Noisy tenant VM causing PCIe AER and host-level resets; 2) GPU hardware degrading (high ECC counts) leading to driver/host instability; 3) recent kernel/driver change triggered sensitivity to transient errors. Prioritize (1) then (2).

jordan: For (1) I've asked cloud provider to show co-tenant list and hypervisor logs. Also requested hypervisor-level PCIe logs and any live migration events. Ticket CP-78321 updated with asks.

mira: I'm adding a short-term monitor to surface PCIe AER and ECC count spikes to the console. Also enabling node-level restart durability to avoid hot loop during retries.

ashley: Customer traffic looks routed to fallback. Latency errors tapering — dashboard now showing error rate back ~baseline for most customers. Keeping mitigation until node replaced.

luis: CS: Customer A confirmed degraded requests are recovering but wants RCA. Flagging for post-mortem.

eng_runtime_tanaka: Can we repro the failure pattern in staging? Recommend we spin a stress VM on the same host family and run memory ECC test, but that's limited on managed infra.

sre_oncall: Action items (short):
- jordan: leave node cordoned and mark for host replacement (ETA 6h) (owner: jordan)
- mira: capture full nvml and dmesg logs and push to incident bucket (owner: mira)
- infra_bot: escalate CP case with hypervisor logs + ask for noisy tenant evidence (owner: infra_bot)
- ashley: keep fallback routing until replacement confirmed (owner: ashley)
- luis: consolidate customer impact statements for RCA (owner: luis)

mira: Uploaded logs to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/2067002468/gpu-host-123/{dmesg,nvidia-smi,syslog}. Also added timeline markers to the incident board.

jordan: Node replacement scheduled by cloud provider for 2026-03-12T07:00Z. If they can't replace, we'll migrate workloads out of the host group.

sre_oncall: For RCA we'll need: full ECC trend by host, hypervisor tenant list, kernel/driver versions, any recent host kernel updates, and confirmation of hardware replacement. Assigning follow-up doc in #postmortems once stabilized.

infra_bot: CP case updated: provider acknowledged multiple AERs on the PCIe bus and will provide hypervisor logs and replacement confirmation. Case ref: CP-78321.

mira: Quick note — I grepped kernel logs; saw repeated "AER: TxE CRC error" entries before the reset. Could be signaling/slot-level noise.

eng_runtime_tanaka: We'll also add an automatic fallback to the model router to avoid hard failures if a node shows >50 corrected AER events in 5m. Filing ticket: INF-1209.

sre_oncall: Handoff: I'll leave this thread open until host replacement completes. If provider confirms noisy tenant, infra will ask for tenant evacuation/host isolation policy. Post-incident RCA will include timeline + mitigation steps + console alerts.

luis: I'll draft the initial customer-facing timeline and share in #customer-communications for review.

mira: Updating incident summary in the board: suspected PCIe/AER-induced GPU instability causing node reboot and pod evictions; fallback routing mitigated customer-visible errors.

jordan: Will verify hardware replacement and post provider confirmation here.

sre_oncall: Thanks team — standing by. If you see repeat events, escalate immediately. :shield:
